title: Stay With Me
mood: A side street at the dome’s foot, a white-gloved hand, and a third question asked in the dark.

hero.alt: On a smoky, ruined street a pink-haired girl and a black-haired girl in school uniform stand back to back, a fist up and a staff raised, two round drones beside them and clawed Enders closing in.

segs.t: Guinevere stood at the board outside the Combat office with a pen in her hand. Two sheets hung there.
The long one listed the new pairs. Aspirants fought in pairs, so on an ordinary raid only pairs went out. The short sheet under it was headed RESERVE.
A cadet with no partner could sign it. The reserve went out as singles, behind the pairs, and cleared up after them.
She signed at the top, in large letters. She had asked nobody else to be her partner. Nobody had asked her.
Layla’s name was not on the sheet.
She won’t stand behind anybody,
Guinevere thought.
She’d rather stay in the VR.
The next morning there were three more names. The last was in small square letters.
Vexana.
To destroy the Enders,
Guinevere thought.
Of course.
For two days she hunted the halls for Vexana, to ask a third time. Vexana was never where she looked.

On the third day the siren sent the reserve to the dome’s foot, a ward of warehouses at the city’s edge. At the end of the main road the dome’s curve met the ground. Enders were climbing in through a split low in it.
The pairs went up the main road. An instructor held the singles at the corner.
“Singles, the side streets,” she said. “Nobody goes alone.”
The others went for the nearest doorway in a bunch. Farther up, one side street ran straight to the split. Three Enders were coming down it, and nobody was going that way.
Top score, and I’m at the back,
Guinevere thought.
I’ll prove myself no matter what!
She ran for the side street.
“Baroque!” the instructor shouted. “Back here!”
She did not look back.

Her drones came up at her shoulders, their rings bright. The first Ender swung at her, and its chest opened with the swing. She ducked and punched the core. A drone hit the second in the face and spun it around, and she finished it.
Let them say that was bought.
She went on up the street alone, toward the split.
A claw came out of a doorway on her right.
It raked her right arm from shoulder to elbow. She clamped her left hand over it. Over her head the drones still burned bright. Her right hand would not close.
She swayed. The ground tipped up to meet her.
When she opened her eyes, someone stood over her, black hair dark against the pale dome. It was Vexana, holding out a white-gloved hand.
“Stay with me, Guinevere.”

blocks.caption: A hand held out through the smoke.

media.alt: Out of gray smoke a black-haired girl in school uniform reaches a white-gloved hand toward the viewer, her long hair streaming and a staff held low in her other hand.

segs.t: Vexana had kept her in sight since the siren.
Nobody goes alone,
the order said. So when Guinevere ran, Vexana went after her. She kept a street’s length back, near enough to shoot and no nearer.
She had seen the claw come out of the doorway. Her arrow had come down one breath too late, and taken the Ender after it struck.
After that, her feet had moved before she decided anything.
Guinevere’s left hand came off the wound. It closed on Vexana’s.
Vexana pulled her to her feet. Guinevere swayed once and stood. She did not let go. Her grip was hard.
For a moment, Vexana did not let go either.
“I had it,” said Guinevere.
“You were on the ground.”
“Resting.”
Down the street, more Enders were squeezing through the split. Guinevere let go and made a fist of her left hand. Her right arm hung. Her drones had not dimmed at all.
Vexana turned and set her back against Guinevere’s. “As long as I’m here, the Aspirant spirit will not fade.”
Against her back, she felt Guinevere laugh.
The Enders came from the split and out of the doorways. Vexana’s staff spat bolts at them. Behind her she heard a fist hit plate, and a drone whine past.
Something moved at Vexana’s left, too close. Before she could turn, a gray drone struck it from the side and knocked it flat.
She covered me,
thought Vexana.
An Ender came down the warehouse wall on Guinevere’s right, her bad side. Its chest opened to strike. Vexana raised her staff.
High over the street, a great arrow of violet light took shape. It fell with a hum, over Guinevere’s shoulder, into the open core.
The street held.
When the last Ender lay still, the pairs came running up from the main road. Guinevere’s back was still against hers, warm, rising and falling fast. Vexana stayed there until it slowed.
The training hall. That night.
The gallery was dark. Vexana sat against its back wall with her practice staff across her knees. She had not lifted it all evening.
Her palm still felt that grip.
I said no so I would never have to watch that,
she thought.
Today I watched it anyway. From a street back, where I couldn’t reach her.
Guinevere would go into the next street alone, and the one after.
Her father had stood in a street like that once, with her behind him. He had stood there alone.
Today they had stood back to back, and each had watched what the other could not see. No claw had come near enough for anyone to step in front of it.
Nobody had ever covered her back before.
On Team-Up Day she had thought,
I’d only bring her the dark.
Today I did,
she thought.
She stood in it with me, and laughed.
At the home she had made one rule of her own.
Nobody stands near me.
She had kept it for years. In that street she had broken it before she decided anything.
If I stay away, she goes alone,
she thought.
If I’m at her back, I see the claw first.
I like her. That’s why it has to be yes.
Below, the door opened. Someone lit the lamp over the heavy bag.
It was Guinevere, her right arm bound from shoulder to elbow. Her two drones bobbed at her shoulders. She did not go to the bag.
For a whole year she had never once looked up.
Tonight she looked up, straight into the dark over the door.
Guinevere climbed the gallery stair. She had never been up it. Her drones went ahead of her, and their yellow rings were the only light.
She had no speech ready. She had tried to make one on the way across the grounds, and every version started
First.
At the top, Vexana stood at the rail with one hand on its edge. A practice staff leaned beside her.
“The medic said to rest,” said Vexana.
“I’m resting. I’m standing very still.”
The drones’ light fell on the staff. Its grip was wound in gray cloth tape.
Guinevere looked at her own knuckles. The same tape. It came from the roll she had found on her jacket, on the worst night of her year.
That was her,
she thought.
She was up here. She saw that night too, and she still said I was strong.
She looked over the rail. Far below, the lamp lit the bag and the worn patch of floor in front of it. From up here you could see every punch.
On the first morning, this girl had walked past her at the gate, eyes front.
All year,
Guinevere thought.
Every night. Me under the lamp, and her up here in the dark.
Guinevere turned from the rail. Only the question was left.
“Will you be my partner?”
Vexana looked at the bound arm. Then she looked at Guinevere. Her fingers closed tighter on the edge of the rail.
“Yes,” said Vexana.
Below, the bag turned a little on its chain.
Not to the name,
Guinevere thought.
To me.
She tried to look dignified. Standing up very straight hurt her arm.
“Training starts tomorrow. No excuses.”
The grin came anyway.
“That’s three,” she said.
“I know,” said Vexana. “I counted.”
Guinevere held out her hand. The left, because the right was bound. It was no way for a lady to shake hands.
Vexana looked at it, the way she had in the courtyard. Then she let go of the rail and took it.
The white glove was still cold from the iron. Guinevere held on until it warmed.
